name: acad-ucs
description: User Coordinate System management: create UCSs from points, objects, views or faces, rotate them about any axis, save and restore them by name. Every drawing tool in the bank works in WCS by default; a UCS is what makes rotated, inclined or sectioned work addressable. See docs/engineering-rules/43-coordinate-systems.md for the contract.
intent_examples: define coordinate system by origin and axes

tools_summary.name: create_ucs_3point
tools_summary.description: Define a UCS from three points: origin, a point on the positive X axis, and a point on the positive-Y side. This is the general case - it fixes origin, rotation and plane in one call. Pass a name to save it; makeCurrent defaults to true.

tools_summary.name: create_ucs_from_entity
tools_summary.description: Align the UCS to an existing entity's own plane and orientation, given its handle. The fastest way to start drawing on something already in the model - a wall face, a sloped polyline, a rotated block.

tools_summary.name: create_ucs_from_view
tools_summary.description: Set the current UCS so its XY plane faces the screen - AutoCAD's UCS View. This is what makes text and dimensions placed on an isometric or a rotated view read straight instead of lying flat on the model's own plane. The origin stays where the current UCS has it, because changing what you are looking at should not move where coordinates are measured from.

tools_summary.name: create_ucs_origin
tools_summary.description: Move the UCS origin without changing its axis directions. The cheapest useful UCS: work near a building corner in small local coordinates instead of large absolute ones.

tools_summary.name: create_ucs_zaxis
tools_summary.description: Define a UCS from an origin and a Z-axis direction; X and Y are derived. Use this for work on an inclined plane - a roof slope, a ramp, a sloped section.

tools_summary.name: delete_ucs
tools_summary.description: Delete a named UCS. The current UCS is unaffected even if it happens to match the deleted definition.

tools_summary.name: get_current_ucs
tools_summary.description: Return the current UCS: origin and the three axis vectors in WCS, plus whether it is the world system. Read-only.

tools_summary.name: list_ucs
tools_summary.description: List every named UCS in the drawing with its origin and axes, plus the current one. Read-only. Call this before restore_ucs to see what names exist.

tools_summary.name: rename_ucs
tools_summary.description: Rename a saved UCS. The new name must be a valid AutoCAD symbol name and must not already exist.

tools_summary.name: restore_ucs
tools_summary.description: Make a previously saved named UCS current. Errors if the name does not exist rather than silently leaving the current UCS in place.

tools_summary.name: rotate_ucs
tools_summary.description: Rotate the current UCS about its own X, Y or Z axis by an angle in degrees. axis is 'x', 'y' or 'z'. Rotating about Z is the usual case: aligning to a wall that does not run north-south.

tools_summary.name: save_ucs
tools_summary.description: Save the current UCS under a name so it can be restored later. Named UCSs are how a multi-storey or multi-wing project keeps its local coordinate systems addressable.

tools_summary.name: set_ucs_previous
tools_summary.description: Step back to the UCS in use before the last change, like AutoCAD's UCS Previous. The history covers changes made through these tools in this session only - a UCS changed by hand in AutoCAD is not in it, and the tool says so rather than silently doing nothing. Reports how many steps remain.

tools_summary.name: set_ucs_world
tools_summary.description: Reset the current UCS to WCS. Every tool in the bank interprets coordinates in WCS by default, so this returns the drawing to the state those tools assume.

tools_summary.name: transform_point
tools_summary.description: Convert one point between coordinate systems. 'from' and 'to' each accept 'world', 'current', or a saved UCS name. Use this to work out WCS coordinates for the drawing tools while they are still WCS-only.
